chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Ali ibn 'Uqba, from his father, from Abu Basir, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both). Anger was mentioned in his presence, so he said:
Surely, a man becomes so angry that nothing ever pleases him, and he enters the Fire because of that.
So when a man becomes angry while he is standing, let him sit, for the wrath of Satan will depart from him. And if he is sitting, let him stand.
And if a man becomes angry at a blood-relative, let him go to him, draw near to him, and touch him; for when a blood-relative touches a blood-relative, he becomes calm.

key_terms.الرحم: Blood-relative, kinship ties; literally 'womb'. The Arabic wordplay in the phrase 'الرحم إذا مست الرحم' uses the same word for both parties, emphasizing the shared origin that makes reconciliation natural.
key_terms.الغضب: Anger — here understood as an emotional state that, left unchecked, can lead to hellfire. The word encompasses both the internal emotional state and its behavioral manifestations.
key_terms.رجز الشيطان: The filth/wrath of Satan — Satan's influence or instigation, here associated with the emotional agitation of anger.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic teaching on managing anger and its spiritual consequences?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) provides practical guidance for managing anger, addressing both its spiritual danger — that uncontrolled anger can lead a person to hellfire — and its physical remedy. He prescribes a change of posture as a physical technique to interrupt the state of anger (sitting if standing, standing if sitting), and specifically for anger toward blood relatives, he recommends physical contact, drawing on the spiritual significance of the word 'rahim' (womb/kinship) as a pacifying force. This hadith was transmitted through a long chain including prominent Shia scholars of Kufa and Qum.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa narrated to us from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. al-Faddal from `Ali b. `Uqba from his father from Abi Basir from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father (as). Anger was mentioned in his presence, so he said:
Surely, a man becomes angry until nothing pleases him, and he enters the Fire due to that.
When a man becomes angry while he is standing, he should sit, for that would cleanse him of the wrath of Satan. If he is sitting, he should stand.
If a man gets angry at a blood-relative, then he should go to him, get near him, and touch him; for if a blood-relative touches a blood-relative [lawfully] he settles down.
